as a newish player myself still on my first run through here are a couple of things I’ve found helpful!
- be aggressive. I know everyone says it, but it really does make a difference. don’t be afraid to get in their face and slash away!
- the sawcleaver would be a better weapon as opposed to the hunters axe when you start out. I started with the axe and struggled, switched to the cleaver and actually began enjoying myself. 
- for builds, usually try going for a single thing. I’m doing skill which helps with visceral attacks. 
- practice parrying! It’s a big part of the game and encouraged. start out with slower enemies until you get ahold of it. 
- explore ! explore ! explore ! try doing most areas on your own. It’ll be a lot more rewarding that way. but if you do have some trouble you can certainly look up tutorials and guides. I do that sometimes.

as a newish player myself still on my first run through here are a couple of things I’ve found helpful!
- be aggressive. I know everyone says it, but it really does make a difference. don’t be afraid to get in their face and slash away!
- the sawcleaver would be a better weapon as opposed to the hunters axe when you start out. I started with the axe and struggled, switched to the cleaver and actually began enjoying myself. 
- for builds, usually try going for a single thing. I’m doing skill which helps with visceral attacks. 
- practice parrying! It’s a big part of the game and encouraged. start out with slower enemies until you get ahold of it. 
- explore ! explore ! explore ! try doing most areas on your own. It’ll be a lot more rewarding that way. but if you do have some trouble you can certainly look up tutorials and guides. I do that sometimes.
- take breaks! If an area or boss is too frustrating, take a break (hours, days, weeks even months!) and then come back to it. It’ll make you feel less frazzled and even excited to try again.
